text:
Alex: Quick ping — running into repeated partial-JSON parse failures in the Python SDK when the SSE stream reconnects after a 429. Not seeing full object boundaries, parser throws on resume. Anyone seen this pattern?
Maya: Yep saw something similar last week; nginx rate-limiter was closing mid-chunk, so client sees truncated event then reconnects. Parser expects complete JSON. :grimacing:
Sam: Are you using the incremental decoder or reading lines? Py client has two paths: `iter_lines()` (line-based) vs incremental NDJSON reassembler. Which one?
Alex: Using our incremental reader `EventStreamDecoder` (wraps `io.BufferedReader`). We call `feed(bytes)` on reconnect but maybe we don't flush buffer.
Jordan: Could be KV-cache resume + partial token prefix. If the server returns 429, do we keep the current kv-prefix and expect a resume token after reconnect? That mismatch would make JSON fragments invalid.
Alex: Server side sends a resume token in `event: resume` usually, but in these 429 cases nginx closes before that event is emitted. So client reconnects without resume token and then receives a continuation chunk starting with `,\"choices\": ...` which is invalid at top level.
Maya: Two options: 1) conservative: drop buffered partial JSON on 4xx and force a fresh response; 2) more permissive: keep buffer and prepend a synthetic `[` or `{` until you see a resume event. Leaning to (1) for safety.
Sam: Agree with (1) from SDK POV — easier and less error-prone. But we should emit a metric so caller can detect extra token cost from drops.
Alex: Implemented quick patch locally: on receiving non-2xx close we discard pending bytes and trigger a resume logic path that requests server to resend prefix. Patch snippet:
```python
# in eventstream/decoder.py
if close_status >= 400 and buffered:
    buffered.clear()  # drop partial JSON to avoid parse errors
    stats.increment("sse.partial_drop")
    # force new stream without reuse of resume token
    self.resume_token = None
```
Jordan: Looks fine. Two ask: 1) add unit that simulates `+ mid-chunk close -> reconnect -> continuation chunk` 2) update CHANGELOG/compat note for behavior change.
Alex: Will add test that feeds `b'{"id":1,"text":"oh'` then EOF then reconnect with `b' world","choices":...}` and assert we don't attempt to parse leftover.
Maya: Also verify rust client behavior — their incremental parser currently concatenates fragments and tolerates leading commas, but Python rejects. We should standardize: SDKs must not try to be permissive.
Sam: FYI, EventBot noticed a deploy of nginx-rate-limiter v2 rolling out during spikes. EventBot: nginx-rate-limiter v2 -> 3 hosts upgraded at 2026-03-16T18:12Z causing early connection resets.
Alex: Good catch, thanks. For immediate fix I'll push the buffer-clear with metric and add a flag `SSE_STRICT = True` defaulting to strict parse.
Jordan: Small nit: make the flag env-configurable and wire to Console so customers can toggle tolerant mode if they have broken proxies.
Alex: Yup. Also adding a small retry-backoff tweak: when we detect a mid-chunk close, use jittered backoff but don't increase token window — this avoids cascading load.
Maya: For QA: can you add a cURL repro for the ops team? Something like:
```bash
# simulate truncated chunk then reconnection
printf 'event: data\ndata: {"msg":"hi' > /tmp/stream.txt
# send then close before finishing
curl -N -X POST "https://staging.redwood.ai/sse" --data-binary @/tmp/stream.txt & sleep 0.1; pkill -f curl
# reconnect and send continuation
printf ' there","end":true}\n' | curl -N -X POST "https://staging.redwood.ai/sse" --data-binary @-
```
Sam: Perfect. I'll open a tiny PR in the python-sdk repo with the patch + metric + test. Assigning to @Maya for review.
Maya: Reviewing now, but schedule looks tight — can we feature-flag behind `SSE_STRICT` so downstream can't break unexpectedly?
Alex: Done. Pushed branch `fix/sse-drop-on-4xx` and linked in PR. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/pull/342
Jordan: I'll coordinate with infra to roll back or patch nginx config on the 3 hosts; ops might prefer header `Keep-Alive: timeout=XX` tuning.
Alex: Thanks team. Follow-ups: Sam add metric dashboard (sse.partial_drop), Maya review PR, Jordan ops plan. I'll post a short postmortem if we see more incidents. :thumbsup:
